correctness.rationale: The source uses the classical forbidden induced P4,C4,2K2 criterion and Behr–Sivaraman–Zaslavsky Proposition 41 classifying all base graphs whose line graphs are threshold. A maximal base graph must have a triangle in its one exceptional component, all spare labels absorbed as pendant edges at a unique triangle center or matched as disjoint edges: without a triangle one can add a suitable edge; with it every omitted base edge violates thresholdness. Choosing a triangle and distinguished center and r paired labels on m=n-3 labels counts binom(n,3)*3*m!/((m-2r)!2^r r!), except the no-pendant case when m is even is triple-counted and needs -2 copies. Exponential involution EGF and matching correction follow by labeled construction; ratio b_{m,r+1}/b_{m,r}=(m-2r)(m-2r-1)/(2(r+1)) strictly decreases, and terminal downweight by 3 preserves log concavity. Independent direct forbidden-four-subgraph enumeration n=3..5 confirmed exact maximal size coefficients; source verifier through n8 was inspected, not assumed a proof.

value.rationale: The maximal-set involution polynomial for a natural Johnson graph family is an exact, reusable invariant with parity-sensitive endpoint correction and strict log-concavity. It distinguishes inclusion-maximal threshold subgraphs from arbitrary threshold graphs and improves on a mere classification by providing all cardinalities and their relative multiplicities; a motivated finite-family enumerator remains valuable without a new general structural theorem.
